✅ **YouTube Live**: [Watch Live](https://youtube.com/watch?v=W-uqWQskV9o)

Currently BPOs don't have a dedicated "place to live". The current BPOs are added to the Fusaka meta EIP https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7607 or added to some personal notes document like https://notes.ethereum.org/@bbusa/fusaka-bpo-timeline, which is not optimal since this does not allow to reference BPOs in a stable way so that it is able to clearly point to where we are on the (BPO-) HF schedule, especially for in-between-main-HF BPOs.

We should come to a consensus here where the independent and stable place for BPOs should be, being it a simple dedicated EIP or another stable GitHub place. Discussion ongoing in #execution-dev channel on R&D.

# Stakers Union Backs EIP-7805 (FOCIL) for Glamsterdam

Stakers Union has [formally voted](https://snapshot.box/#/s:stakersunion.eth/proposal/0x458f07933cae3daff239f4acbf9414411c752aedd4957d73480b177c497931a9) to support EIP-7805: Fork-choice enforced Inclusion Lists (FOCIL) for inclusion in the next Ethereum network upgrade, Glamsterdam. We believe FOCIL measurably improves censorship resistance, reduces builder centralization risk, and strengthens solo-validator sovereignty without adding undue operational burden to home stakers.

[**Read More**](https://www.stakersunion.com/eip-7805)
X Stream: https://x.com/i/broadcasts/1jMJgRYBoOOGL

Here is @OffchainLabs Prysm team’s stance on Glamsterdam’s non-headliner consensus EIP selection:
 
* **EIP-8045: Exclude slashed validators from proposing**
  We support 8045 only if this is on top of Fusaka and proposer look ahead field exists in beacon state

* **EIP-7688: Forward compatible consensus data structures**
  We support 7688 now. Ideally, this should go out alongside or after the execution layer SSZ transition, but given current priorities, the consensus layer should not wait.

* **EIP-8071: Prevent using consolidations as withdrawals** / **EIP-8061: Increase exit and consolidation churn**
  We prefer 8061 over 8071 for the reasons below. We agree that using the consolidation queue for withdrawals is a bug that needs fixing. Between the two, 8071 is one fix, but 8061 is a cleaner approach since it allows the queue to be borrowed, which improves UX with 0x03 builders in ePBS.
  Our hesitation with 8061 is security: we want a stronger analysis showing that shortening the WS period is still safe under 4x withdrawal churn and 2x consolidation churn. Decision tree:
  * **If** 8061 is proven sound, we prefer 8061 over 8071
  * **Else If** if 8071 is chosen, we suggest adding the shared queue concept
  * **Otherwise**, we’re fine sticking with 8071 as is

* **EIP-8062: Add sweep withdrawal fee for 0x01 validators** / **EIP-8068: Neutral effective balance design**
  We’re against both. For 8062, setting the right fee is tough because node operators have different tolerances, and the tradeoff between too high or too low is hard to balance. For 8068, the added complexity worries us: new fields in the beacon state and more process epoch changes. It’s also unclear either EIP would meaningfully push operators to consolidate, and we don’t want consensus changes we’re not confident in.

* **EIP-7805: FOCIL**
  We’re neutral on 7805 but want to flag the added complexity of bundling FOCIL with ePBS, which may delay Glamsterdam’s mainnet timeline
Here's RIG's view on non-headliner CL EIP prioritization for Glamsterdam: https://notes.ethereum.org/@css/rig-glamsterdam.

**Heka-Bogotá upgrade** headliner discussions can likely start in January (at the latest), assuming Glamsterdam scope is wrapped up in November or early December. (Based on https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/reconfiguring-allcoredevs/23370#p-56785-network-upgrade-timelines-8).

**Minimum mainnet timeline from testnet releases** 
(based on https://github.com/ethereum/pm/blob/master/processes/protocol-upgrade.md)

| Event | Min days | Total elapsed |
|-------|------------|---------------|
| testnet release(s) |   | 0  |
| 1st testnet upgrade |  14 | 14 |
| 2nd testnet upgrade | 14 | 28 |
| mainnet date set | 2 | 30 |
| mainnet client releases | 7 | 37 |
| mainnet upgrade | 30 | 67|

_Completely hypothetical mainnet targets (for illustration purposes only)_
**Glamsterdam**: June 24, 2026, testnet release(s) required by April 18, 2026 (at the latest).
**Heka-Bogotá**: December 9, 2026, testnet release(s) required by October 3, 2026 (at the latest). 
*Note 2026 is a Devcon year

> * For 8062, setting the right fee is tough because node operators have different tolerances, and the tradeoff between too high or too low is hard to balance.

@terencechain Could you expand on what you mean here. We want node operators to switch from `0x01` to `0x02` to achieve fast finality on a reasonable timeline. It is hard for me to understand why we would in this context wish to wait with setting up reasonable incentives for consolidation. It might lead to too drastic efforts at a later date. Specifically, for the two scenarios:

- Undershooting: If we undershoot, it would be very positive that we will have implemented the EIP already in Glamsterdam. We would then have the logic needed for consolidation and can simply raise the fee by adjusting `WITHDRAWAL_FEE_FRACTION` for the next hardfork. If we think that we might underestimate the required incentive, and undershoot, it is great to have two forks available for tuning, instead of trying to catch up when it's too late.
- Overshooting: Node operators will still need to transition to `0x02`. And the fees we are considering are still at such a low level that operators might care more about queue length and factor that into their decision on when to migrate (in other words, there is no scenario where the queues become unmanageable).

My general point would be that we have a rather broad range of fees that are acceptable for EIP-8062. The mere fact that we cannot directly pinpoint an optimal fee is not a reason to DFI. It is rather the opposite. It is a reason to proceed with a reasonable fee already in G*, because it might not be any easier to make a first guess for H*, and it can then be more consequential to be wrong.

@anderselowsson  I am slightly concerned about adding code to consensus that may not achieve the expected result even though the change itself is relatively simple, do you foresee this as absolutely necessary and that community pressure alone will not be enough for node operators to consolidate. I do agree that if we are planning to do it in the H* fork then it’s better to do it sooner rather than later, and if we do it, I personally think it’s better to overshoot than undershoot

@terencechain , also, the relative APY versus competitors is what really matters for large NOs, since it determines who “wins” more stake.
We’ve already seen with proposer-timing games that just a few basis points can make one NO outperform others on profitability.
My intuition is that even a very conservative fee will still create enough pressure to migrate to 0x03 simply to preserve APY parity.
To me this feels like the simplest thing we can do, and then, I'd support 8061 as I think it elegantly speeds up exits without big compromises.

Lighthouse have made our early preferences known [here](https://blog.sigmaprime.io/glamsterdam-eip-preferences.html) and I'll summarise below. 

Considered for Inclusion
- EIP-7805: Fork-Choice Inclusion Lists (FOCIL) (CL) - Support inclusion.

Proposed for Inclusion
- EIP-7688: Forward compatible consensus data structures - Do not support inclusion.
- EIP-8045: Exclude slashed validators from proposing - Do not support inclusion.
- EIP-8061: Increase churn limits - Support either this EIP or 8071 for inclusion, with the preference for 8071.
- EIP-8062: Add sweep withdrawal fee for 0x01 validators (CL) - Do not support inclusion.
- EIP-8068: Neutral effective balance design (CL) - Do not support inclusion.

We're noting that there aren't any EIPs here we think are necessarily bad ideas, just that ePBS + FOCIL is going to be a big ask for delivery mid-next year as it is, so we're being very cautious about supporting additional EIPs. 

I will also add that our internal discussions came to a similar viewpoint to the one Terence expressed above for 8062 and 8068. We see these as having significant complexity/friction for not a lot of apparent gain. We agree consolidation is an important goal, we'd like to see it pushed harder than as proposed. That is, if we're going to incentivise the switch, let's do so meaningfully. Saying that, if there's modelling or a strong argument that this change gets us closer to consolidation targets than we have interpreted, we could be persuaded.

Here to reiterate Diva Staking’s support for including **EIP-7688 in Glamsterdam.**

Why now: 
Including EIP-7688 now stabilizes generalized indices and SSZ merkleization across forks, preventing Merkle-proof breakage when fields are added. It comes with no security reduction, so we pay a one-time migration cost to gain long-term forward compatibility.

It also doesn’t interfere with ePBS, which is already scheduled for inclusion in the hard fork. While ePBS introduces several CL containers, the impact from 7688 is controlled. Practically, it’s the same trade-off: bundle 7688 with ePBS to ship a stable baseline now, or ship ePBS first and rework again when 7688 lands.

Bringing up prior support to EIP7688 inclusion:
- **Lido**, @dgusakov: https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/1754#issuecomment-3410880980
- **Diva Staking**: https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/1754#issuecomment-3409601784

> * Our hesitation with 8061 is security: we want a stronger analysis showing that shortening the WS period is still safe under 4x withdrawal churn and 2x consolidation churn. Decision tree:

@terencechain Do you mean a more detailed analysis that shows that the weak subjectivity period is indeed only reduced to 7 days, or an analysis showing that 7 days is fine? As for the former, I have a maxeb note that explains the weak subjectivity effect of the various operations, and can put it all together in a document accompanying the EIP (or further expand the security section) if it helps. What I can briefly say here is that it might seem like there's a mistake because the period is only reduced by 2.24x even though we're doubling consolidations and 4xing exits, but you have to consider that:
- the withdrawal delay adds a fixed 27 hours to the weak subjectivity period, so really the "dynamic part" (churn dependent) of the WS period is reduced from ~14.6 to 5.9, a bigger reduction (~2.47x)
- 4x the exit churn has the same effect as a 3x of the activation + exit churn, because each unit of exit churn has twice the impact of a unit of activation churn (=> 1 unit of activation+exit churn = 2/3 exit + 1/3 activation, so 4x the exit churn gets us  to 8/3 + 1/3 = 3). Consolidation churn is a a bit more than 1/2 of the current total churn (`balance_churn_limit`), since one unit of consolidation churn = one unit of activation+exit churn, so we're 2xing ~half of the churn and 3xing ~the other half => ~2.5x effect, exactly what the formula shows

If what you're interested in is the latter, I am not sure how we can conclusively say that one week is "still safe". It's not safe if the definition of safety is that you only need to be online once every two weeks if you want the slashability decay in case of attack to be bounded by 10%. It is safe if you're fine with the slashability decay to be bounded by 20% instead, or if you're fine with being online once a week. I don't know how to conclusively determine what is "necessary". Directionally, it seems clear to me that the current weak subjectivity period is way too long, and one week seems perfectly fine for the kind of security guarantees that it is providing.

Portmanteau needed for Heka + Bogotá upgrade after Glamsterdam (only if there is time after Glamsterdam scoping discussion)

https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/portmanteau-for-heka-bogota-upgrade-after-glamsterdam/26400

> I am slightly concerned about adding code to consensus that may not achieve the expected result even though the change itself is relatively simple, do you foresee this as absolutely necessary and that community pressure alone will not be enough for node operators to consolidate. I do agree that if we are planning to do it in the H* fork then it’s better to do it sooner rather than later, and if we do it, I personally think it’s better to overshoot than undershoot

@terencechain  Yes I am very much against community pressure alone for solving a problem that ultimately comes down to having the right incentives in place. As an example, I've heard some node operators have smart contracts depending on 0x01 that are frozen (legal, etc.), so that ETH will hardly move over to `0x02` unless there is an incentive to do so. A small fee is smoother than a twitter blame game.

> We agree consolidation is an important goal, we'd like to see it pushed harder than as proposed. That is, if we're going to incentivise the switch, let's do so meaningfully. Saying that, if there's modelling or a strong argument that this change gets us closer to consolidation targets than we have interpreted, we could be persuaded.

@jking-aus Flagging that EIP-8062 was updated yesterday with an alternative specification that has a higher fee, to also address the lower capital efficiency of `0x02` validators. So there is an alternative with a more meaningful incentive, that still is motivated theoretically from a pure fairness perspective. Quick summary [here](https://x.com/weboftrees/status/1988777606989385957?s=20).
Lodestar just published thoughts here on EIP inclusion: https://blog.chainsafe.io/lodestar-glamsterdam-upgrade-proposal/ TL;DR:

Nimbus's views: https://notes.status.im/s/6-ZIuquGe

tl;dr we support EIP-7688 and EIP-8045. There's conditional support for EIP-7805.
Teku team's view on EIP inclusion: https://hackmd.io/KUFN0UIMRgCLheMVzFmN5A

Grandine prefers to ship Glamstendarm ASAP so we would prefer to have only ePBS, which will be a huge effort even without additional EIPs. We would be happy to include FOCIL if ePBS turns out to be significantly easier than the current estimate.
closing in lieu of #1812
